series.title: One Piece
series.verdict: The one I will still be watching when I am old. Nobody builds a world like Oda, and nobody else can make a goodbye to a *boat* land like that.

entries.title: East Blue
entries.note: Slow to start and worth every minute. Introduces the trick the whole series runs on: give a character one impossible dream and never let them drop it.

entries.title: Arlong Park
entries.note: The first time the show stops being funny for twenty minutes and proves it can hurt. Nami's arc is still the cleanest thing in it.

entries.title: Alabasta
entries.note: Big, hot, and the first proper war. Crocodile is the template every good One Piece villain has copied since.

entries.title: Water 7 / Enies Lobby
entries.note: My favourite stretch of anything, ever. It asks whether the crew actually wants each other, and then answers it with a burning flag.

entries.title: Thriller Bark
entries.note: Filler-shaped but not filler. Pays off enormously later, which is very One Piece of it.

entries.title: Marineford
entries.note: The one that broke the fandom. Watch it in as few sittings as you can manage.

entries.title: Wano
entries.note: Too long and I did not care. Some of the best-looking animation in television is in here.

entries.title: Egghead
entries.note: Keeping up week to week for the first time in my life. Different, tense, and very good.

series.title: Naruto
series.verdict: The first anime I was properly obsessed with. Uneven, overstuffed, and it still gets me every single time the flute music starts.

entries.title: Land of Waves
entries.note: Zabuza and Haku in twelve episodes. Better written than most of what follows and it is episode 6.

entries.title: Chunin Exams
entries.note: Peak tournament arc. Rock Lee versus Gaara is the fight I have rewatched most in my life.

entries.title: Sasuke Retrieval
entries.note: Five fights, five losses, one broken friendship. The end of Part 1 does not pretend anything is fine.

entries.title: Shippuden: Rescue Gaara
entries.note: Great return. Sets the tone that the Akatsuki are a problem you cannot punch your way out of.

entries.title: Shippuden: Pain's Assault
entries.note: The high point of Shippuden. Everything the show has been saying about cycles of revenge, said properly.

entries.title: Shippuden: Fourth Great Ninja War
entries.note: Enormous, exhausting, and full of filler. There is a great forty-episode arc buried in here somewhere.

series.title: Bleach
series.verdict: The best-looking of the three and the one with the least interest in explaining itself. *Thousand-Year Blood War* turned it from a fond memory into something I actively recommend.

entries.title: Soul Society
entries.note: Rescue arc, tournament structure, and a cast where the side characters are cooler than the hero. Aizen's reveal still works.

entries.title: Arrancar / Hueco Mundo
entries.note: Some incredible fights spread very thin. The pacing is where a lot of people quit, and I understand why.

entries.title: Fullbring
entries.note: The one everyone forgets. Interesting idea — a hero with nothing left — undercut by having to reset it.

entries.title: Thousand-Year Blood War
entries.note: A studio deciding to prove a point. Ruthless, gorgeous, and it finally lets the manga's ending look as good as it read.

series.title: Dragon Ball
series.verdict: Not one of the Big 3 — it is the reason the Big 3 exist. Half comedy adventure, half the loudest fights ever drawn.

entries.title: Dragon Ball (original)
entries.note: Funnier and weirder than people remember. Kid Goku hunting for magic balls is a completely different show and it rules.

entries.title: Saiyan Saga
entries.note: The turn. Twenty-something episodes where the good guys lose almost everything, and Piccolo gets the best moment in the franchise.

entries.title: Frieza Saga
entries.note: Yes, it takes forever. It is also the single most famous transformation in anime, and it earns it.

entries.title: Cell Saga
entries.note: Gohan's arc is the emotional peak of Z, and the ending genuinely commits to something.

entries.title: Buu Saga
entries.note: Silly in a way I did not appreciate as a kid and love now. Fusion dance included.

entries.title: Dragon Ball Super
entries.note: Wildly inconsistent. The Tournament of Power is worth the ticket on its own.
